iii Course Introduction Jesus commanded his disciples, “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age.” (Matthew 28:19-20) The command of our Lord Jesus Christ is very clear; make disciples. Then he makes clear the process of making disciples: to go, to baptize (evangelize), and to teach them to observe all that he has commanded us. And then he encourages us with the promise to be with us in the task…even to the end of the age. Paul, the apostle, in a letter to Timothy makes clear a principle that enables Jesus’ command to be fulfilled through all who know him…the principle of multiplication. “and what you have heard me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others also.” (2 Timothy 2:2) One-to-One Discipleship Training was designed to encourage this principle of multiplication and to help you fulfill the command of our Lord to make disciples! Here are some practical steps:  Study this material with a facilitator for your own understanding and spiritual growth.  Take Evangelism and Discipleship 2 offered by BEE to learn how to use this material to make your own disciples.  Think and pray about someone who can benefit from studying this course. v  Plan to meet with this person on a regular basis (at least once a week). Study and discuss each lesson together with the goal of good understanding and personal application. The joys will be many as you help this person build a confident and mature relationship with Jesus and to enable this person to help others also.

DESCRIPTION OF THE COURSE

This course provides three systematic approaches to fulfill this command. Unit 1 is designed to help new believers or unbelievers understand who Jesus is or believe in him by introducing him to them. If you do not know who Jesus is, or if you are not sure of your salvation, study this unit carefully with your facilitator. We recommend you studying this unit even if you already accepted Jesus as your Savior and Lord. The more knowledge you have of the truth of the gospel the easier it will be to share this truth with unbelievers. Unit 2 introduces the importance of a devotional Bible study or Quiet Time. A Christian cannot grow spiritually without interacting with the word of God. God’s word is spiritual nourishment for the believer. Study this unit and make Quiet Time a part of your life. You will experience spiritual growth through reading, meditating, and applying the word of God in your daily Quiet Time. Unit 3 deals with topics essential to Christian living that will equip you in areas important for spiritual maturity. Remember that the knowledge you learn from this course is not enough to change your life. Your daily trusting in Christ, your commitment, and your practice of that knowledge will help make the change (Hebrews 5:12-14). Whatever you learn start practicing immediately. It is our desire that you grow spiritually and bear fruit that you might produce a hundredfold as a disciple of Christ (Mark 4:1-9).

COURSE OBJECTIVES

1. Explain who Jesus is, what he has done, and what he is doing now. 2. Know and believe that Jesus is your Savior and Lord. 3. Know how to interact daily with the word of God. 4. Understand the importance of the following areas to your spiritual growth and maturity in Christ: assurance of salvation, the attributes of vi God, the word of God, prayer, fellowship, evangelism, Spirit-filled life, temptation, obedience, and ministry.

LESSON ORGANIZATION Each lesson is divided into the following parts: Title, Lesson Introduction, Lesson Outline, Lesson Objectives, Assignments, and Lesson Development. The title, introduction, outline, and objectives provide a preview of the lesson. The lesson assignments describe specific tasks within the lesson to help accomplish the objectives. Lesson Development provides comments and questions to move the student toward the objectives. Please give careful attention to every part of the lessons. Read all comments and answer to all questions. These will fix your attention once more on the main points of the lesson. This procedure is designed to make your learning more effective and longer lasting. Make special note of the charts and other illustrations. These illustrations will help you to identify with those who followed Jesus vii sharing in both the hardships and the joys of letting the tremendous truths of the gospel grip your heart. Also, you will find these illustrations useful in your preaching and teaching. viii Student Instructions In each lesson there are assignments to be fulfilled before you study the lesson with your facilitator in order to satisfactorily complete the lesson. The following gives a list of differing types of assignments with a general description: Lesson preparation. The purpose of this assignment is to use your time with facilitator effectively as well as to make you understand the content of the lesson before you study it with your facilitator. You and your facilitator are committing valuable time for this training. It is our desire that both of you use this time most efficiently. The most important purpose of this training is not transferring the knowledge in this workbook. As Jesus spent his time with his disciples so that they could learn from his teaching and life, you need to spend quality time with your facilitator together through this workbook to grow as Jesus’ disciple. When you prepare for the lesson by answering all the questions in the lesson, you are ready to spend more meaningful time with your facilitator beyond acquiring knowledge. You must look for the given passages to answer most questions. We recommend you writing down the passages you look for on a separate notebook. By doing so, not only will you prepare for the training as a student but also as a facilitator in the future. Scripture memory. The purpose of this assignment is to build into your heart and mind Scriptures that will strengthen you in your daily walk with Jesus. In each lesson you will be asked to memorize verses of Scripture related to the content of the lesson. Choose a translation of the ix Bible you are reading consistently. Take sermon notes from a worship service. The purpose of this assignment is to encourage you toward regular worship with other believers and attentiveness to the message given each week. As you attend a weekly worship service, bring paper and pen to write down what you learn from the sermon given by the pastor. Daily Bible reading. The purpose of this assignment is to encourage in your life a habit of daily Bible reading. Starting with Unit III you are asked to read a certain number of chapters from the Bible each week. Daily Quiet Time (QT). The purpose of this assignment is to help you develop a daily time alone with the Lord and his word. Unit II will give you practical helps to make this a meaningful source of daily strengthening in the Lord and your walk with him. A part of this assignment will be to record what you are learning in a Quite Time notebook. You will need a separate notebook for this purpose. Memorize the names of all the books of the Bible. The purpose of this assignment is to make you very familiar with the whole Bible and to more easily know where to find passages of Scripture. x UNIT 1 Encounter 1. Who Is Jesus Christ? 2. ASSIGNMENTS

1. Study this lesson by answering all questions. 2. Memorize Acts 2:32. No one in all of history has had such an impact on this world as Jesus Christ did. No one in all of history lived a completely sinless life, died on a cross, rose from the grave, and conquered death. Jesus’ death is an astonishing expression of his love for us. However if the death of Jesus on the cross marked the end of his life, he would have eventually become a vague memory, no different than any other great historical figure. Indeed the Bible clearly shows that Jesus not only died on the cross but that he also rose from the dead. Jesus was resurrected and is still alive and relevant to us today. Praise the Lord! 11 12 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training There are some people who acknowledge that Jesus existed, lived his life, and then died. These same people choose to reject the truth and power of the resurrection; hence they are unable to know Christ fully. Christ prophesied of his resurrection while he was ministering among the people. Furthermore the resurrection was the crux or central point of the disciples’ testimony. The disciples and others were so convicted of the truth of the resurrection of Jesus that they risked their own lives for the sake of sharing the good news (gospel).

Defining Quiet Time Objective 1: Define Quiet Time in your own words When we receive Christ and become a Christian and also have an assurance of salvation, a personal relationship is formed with Christ. Just as we need to associate with people to deepen our relationships, a personal fellowship with Christ is necessary to deepen our relationship with him. The time when such association is made on a personal basis is referred to as either Quiet Time (QT) or time of devotion.

Examine what kind of relationship you have with Jesus Christ. Is

Jesus close to you? Do you meet him regularly? Quiet Time provides a way to be with him. Let us look to Jesus and his example of Quiet Time.

Quiet Time ● 25 This is what is referred to as a time of devotion or what is commonly called a Quiet Time (QT). #### B. Reasons for Quiet Time Objective 2: Explain reasons why a regular Quiet Time is important to the Christian Why do Christians have QT? Why is it important to be quiet before God? See the following for possible reasons Christians may have for spending QT with God: To have a personal relationship with God. The relationship with God cannot be broken once it is established (Romans 8:39). But to deepen this relationship, continuous fellowship is necessary. There are several ways of having fellowship with God; we can have a personal and intimate fellowship with him through QT. To receive the guidance and protection of God. We will gain more knowledge and understanding of him as he provides insight and answers to problems in our daily lives through his Holy Spirit and his word.
Question 5: How do the following verses describe the guidance and
protection of God? a) Psalm 119:105 b) Psalm 119:133 God provides concrete answers to the problems in our daily lives through QT. To learn how to be more like Christ in his character, personality, and life (2 Corinthians 3:18). For Christians to be the ‘salt and light’ of the world and spread the gospel, we should be true examples of the Christian faith. We need a personal relationship with God if we desire for our lives and personality to be transformed. To carry out the Lord's work (Luke 5:15-16; Mark 1:35). To do the works assigned in the church and to carry out the duty of spreading the gospel in the world, it is imperative to receive power and direction through fellowship with God. 26 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training #### C. Preparation for Quiet Time Objective 3: Describe how to prepare Quiet Time practically 1. Your Mind You are about to have fellowship with God, the Almighty Creator. Prepare your mind with expectation and fear. In this case, the fear is related to reverence to God. It is a combination of love and respect for an awesome God. 2. The Bible and QT Notebook Open your Bible to the passage on which you will meditate for the day's QT. We recommend you to have QT systematically. Once you start a book in the Bible for your QT, continue the book until you finish it. Normally one paragraph is appropriate for a day's QT. If it is too short, you can continue to the next paragraph. If it is too long, you can stop in the middle of the paragraph. Be flexible on the amount for a day's QT. Sometimes the Holy Spirit teaches enough lessons from one verse. If that is the case, stop there and continue with the remaining verses on the next day. Be ready to write down what the Holy Spirit impresses on you in your QT notebook. Use the format provided at the end of this lesson for recording your insights. Do not use any secondary material for your QT. You need to have direct fellowship with the Holy Spirit through his word. 3. Place and Time The place for your QT is very important. You want to have a personal fellowship with the Lord, and you do not want to be disturbed. Find a place where you can spend twenty to thirty minutes with God without any disturbance. Time often plays a crucial role in having consistent QT. Usually early morning is the most appropriate time for QT because you can start a new day with his guidance. However the time for QT is flexible depending on one’s situation. The important thing is to make sure the time for QT is not sacrificed because of other urgent matters in your life and ministry. Quiet Time ● 27 #### D. Suggested Method for Quiet Time Objective 4: Know how to do Quiet Time by yourself The purpose of QT is not to understand the Scriptures thoroughly but to have God speak to you through his word. You can start QT using the following steps: 1. Praise God Start your QT with praise. To praise God means to commend him for all that he has done. Please read Psalm 59:17 for an example of praising God. You can praise God in prayer, while singing songs at church, while listening to praise music, or while meditating on the Psalms, such as Psalm 98. Praise prepares the heart to go before God. 2. Depend on the Holy Spirit The Holy Spirit is the author of the Bible, which was written through his inspiration. Therefore he illumines us to understand the Scriptures. 3. Find Truths by Meditating on the Word God wants to reveal himself to us through the Scriptures (giving comfort, hope, warning, direction, etc.). Therefore we need to meditate on the words he gives us each day. During your QT, read the given text several times. Read his words with humility before God and the respect for his authority. Also, the more we meditate upon God’s word, the more our minds become focused on his eternal truths. Meditate on the Scripture and find his eternal truths like the following: 1) Sins to confess 2) Promises to keep

3) Examples to follow

4) Actions to take 5) Knowledge on God, Jesus Christ, or the Holy Spirit Remember an English word, SPEAK. Allow the Holy Spirit to SPEAK to you through his word. The Holy Spirit sometimes may illumine several truths from one verse, and sometimes none. Remember that you do not have to understand everything in the passage, but you need to listen to what the Holy Spirit is speaking to you through the passage at that moment. You may have to read the same verse several times over in order 28 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training to find truths. This may seem repetitive at first, but as you become familiar with the method, you will be able to find truths more quickly. It takes time to make the method yours, do not give up! 4. Lesson 1. Assurance of Salvation ● 37

Your confident and positive answers indicate that you are sure of your salvation. Becoming a Christian involves receiving Jesus Christ by faith. It is the gift of God's love and forgiveness. It results in a threefold commitment of a person to Christ of one’s intellect, emotions, and will. In other words, it is a commitment of the whole being. Our relationship with Christ can be analogous to the concept of marriage, which must also contain the same three ingredients. For example, a man may be convinced intellectually that the woman who is his intended bride is the “right” spouse for him. He may be involved emotionally and love her with all his heart, but marriage requires more than the intellect and the emotions. It also involves the will. Not until the man and the woman, as an act of the will, commit themselves to each other before a minister do they become husband and wife. The two words, “I do,” make all the difference. So it is with your relationship with Jesus Christ. It is neither enough to believe intellectually in Christ, nor is it enough to have an emotional experience. Though both are valid, you do not become a Christian until, as an act of the will, you trust Jesus Christ as your Savior and Lord. Let us examine each of the three elements of Christian commitment. Objective 2: Understand the threefold commitment of the intellect, emotion, and will in your salvation #### A. Commitment of the Intellect Christianity is not “a blind leap of faith.” It is built upon historical facts, documented by centuries of scholarship and research. Many leading scholars have dedicated their lives to investigating the life, teachings, death, resurrection, and influence of Jesus of Nazareth. As a result, we have more historical evidence proving his resurrection than we have proof that Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo. This good news of Jesus Christ’s resurrection was the message of the revolutionary New Testament church. It is still a revolutionary message today. It is a fact of history. In order to make an intellectual commitment, we need to have a clear understanding of the gospel recorded in the Bible. Now let us determine if we have understanding of both the gospel and its historical facts. 38 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training 1. Who is Jesus Christ?

#### B. Commitment of the Emotion An emotion is a feeling or reaction to a specific act, event or experience. Having been created with emotions, we experience emotional reactions in the process of hearing the gospel of Jesus, coming to know him, and believing in him. However the failure to distinguish between different emotions has caused many people to be confused in their relationship with God. 1. Emotion Varies As human beings, emotions are a normal part of our lives. Different personalities obviously produce varying reactions. One person may have high emotional energy, while another may be calm and reserved. Because emotions vary greatly, they should not be depended upon. Even though we all need to experience God, seeking an emotional experience has caused many to lack the assurance of a vital relationship with God. 2. Emotion as a Result of Faith Assurance is based on the authority of God's word. When you meet God's conditions, as revealed in his word, you can be assured that you are a child of God. The Christian lives by faith in the trustworthiness of God himself and his word. The train diagram illustrates the relationship between fact (God and his word), faith (our trust in God and his word), and feeling (the results of our experience). Note the three components in the diagram. The engine is in the front to pull the train. The firebox that contains the heat source or fuel follows the engine. The last one is a caboose. The train will run with the power of steam produced in the engine using the heat source from the firebox. The engine cannot pull the train if the fuel is not provided. The train will run with or without the caboose, but it would be useless to attempt to pull the train by the caboose. 40 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training

FACT FAITH FEELING

In the Christian life, fact is the engine, faith is the heat source, and feeling is the caboose. When we, as Christians, add our faith on the fact which is the word of God, our believing life can go forward. As the caboose cannot pull the train, we should not depend upon feelings or emotions. Instead, we must place our faith in the trustworthiness of God and the promises of his word. #### C. Commitment of the Will In addition to the intellect and emotions, becoming a Christian and being certain that you are a Christian involves the will. Christ emphasized the importance of one’s will in relation to the assurance of salvation. A Christian must make a conscious commitment to believe in and to follow Jesus Christ.

The Holy Spirit counsels us to have such faith (Romans 8:16), but as we begin our spiritual journey with this personal conviction, we need objective facts about the God in whom we have placed our faith. Abstract and philosophical conceptions of God will no longer suffice. We need to know our God more deeply. Only with clearer knowledge will our faith become stronger. As Christians, we already know God. However if God is to be the constant center of our lives, we need to know more about God's attributes. Only then will we be able to live in a manner pleasing to God. The Bible teaches very specifically about God's attributes. Many people live a life of doubt and unbelief because they do not know God's character. Knowing God is very important as we live our lives. If we do not know him, it is easy to commit wrong, since it is difficult to understand the circumstances and direction of our lives without the knowledge of God. The mightiest thoughts the mind can entertain are the thoughts of God. But our ideas concerning God should correspond to that which is true of God. Only then can we truly worship and lead a genuine Christian life.

Objective 1: Describe the brief history of the formation of the Bible 51 52 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training The Bible is a compilation of books written by around forty authors in a period spanning 1,500 years. The Old Testament is the word that Moses and the prophets received from God. It has been handed down orally or in writing through history. The Pentateuch was established as the authorized version in the fifth century BC; the books of the prophets and the books of literature in the second century BC. The Old Testament is composed of thirty-nine books and is written mostly in Hebrew. The New Testament is a compilation of books and letters written by the disciples who were inspired by God. Recognition of a formal canon of the New Testament did not occur until long after the time of its writing. The collection and recognition of all the New Testament books was a gradual process. During the first century of the church (from Pentecost to about AD 140), there was only a very slow distribution and recognition of the writings that later were brought together and recognized as inspired. After AD 140 a more rapid recognition of the canonical books occurred. By the end of the second century almost all of the books were known and recognized as authoritative. Finally, by the end of the fourth century the official canon of the New Testament was recognized and fixed. Why did it take so long for the authority of all the New Testament books to be acknowledged by the church? First, the New Testament church already had a canon of Scripture—the Old Testament—which was considered all that was needed in the church ―for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16). Second, as long as the apostles were alive, there was little felt need for an authoritative body of writings. The early church already had the Old Testament and the living apostles to teach them (Acts 2:42). There was no urgency to copy and distribute the New Testament books so that they could be widely known and acknowledged. Third, the recipients of the New Testament books were spread all across the Mediterranean basin. It is likely that churches would share with other churches any authoritative books that they received from the apostles. But because of poor communication and the slow production of books, no single church would always know about all of the apostolic writings in existence. Churches would receive various portions of the New Testament without knowing what portions other churches possessed.

Lesson 3. Word of God: The Bible ● 53

The New Testament is composed of twenty-seven books and was, in the original manuscripts, written entirely in Greek. The Bible’s purpose is not only to educate us or give us mere knowledge, but it is also to teach us knowledge about the saving grace of God and how to walk with God in our daily lives.

Review the names of the books in the New Testament. Prayer is the natural overflow of meaningful time in Scripture. Prayer to God completes the fellowship element in your relationship with him. Respond back to God in prayer after he speaks to you through his word. In this manner, you share your heart with the One who longs for your companionship. Prayer is how the power of God is unleashed. Personal battles and battles for others are won in prayer, and the cause of Christ is thus furthered. Through prayer, you have the power and the privilege to be used by God to help change lives. We do not avail ourselves of this power primarily because of our unbelief. The disciples of the first century knew how to pray and claimed in faith the power of our omnipotent God to help change the course of history. We serve the same powerful God today and we too are able to call upon him in prayer. #### A. What Is Prayer? Objective 1: Define prayer in your own words by comparing similar things in other religions Prayer is simply communicating with God. It is a dialogue between two who love each other—God and human. As children of God, we are invited to draw near to the throne of grace with confidence (Hebrews 4:16). To know exactly what prayer is, we need to know about the widely held misconceptions regarding prayer.

Lesson 4. Prayer ● 63

1. Prayer is not meditation by oneself. Prayer is offered to the living God. 2. Prayer is different from requesting to other gods in other religions. Prayer can only be offered in his name by those who believe in Christ (John 16:24). 3. Prayer is not just about making requests. The main purpose of prayer is to deepen our relationship with God. 4. Prayer is not just offered in public but starts in a private room (Matthew 6:6). 5. Prayer is not repeating meaningless religious words. Prayer is the deliverance of specific intentions.

To Glorify God (John 14:13) We glorify God when we remember who he is and what he has done for us during prayer. 3. The Fellowship of Christians Objective 4: List the characteristics of Christian fellowship 1. Be Members of One Another So we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually members one of another. (Romans 12:5) If it is true that everyone is equal under the cross, every Christian has the privilege of becoming an integral member of the family of God. In the family of God, we must be willing to learn from one another and to encourage one another. The fellowship of the saints can fully develop only when Christians are diligent in building one another up. We cannot participate in this fellowship while isolating ourselves from the community of saints. God desires that all Christians become active members of God's family by joining a local church. The New Testament states that Christians are “members one of another.” Paul used an illustration to get this point across—the human body.
Question 6: Read 1 Corinthians 12:14-27. Summarize the conclusion Paul
comes to in these verses. 1 Corinthians 12:27 2. Be United in Christ There is one body and one Spirit—just as you were called to the one hope that belongs to your call— (Ephesians 4:4) The human body is not made up of separate and individual members. Rather, the body exists as a unified whole of many parts that are members of one body. Similarly, the church is not an association of individual Christians but is the body of Christ, consisting of people who are members of one another from the inception of their Christian lives. In its broadest sense, the body of Christ is the historical and global community of the saints. The Bible frequently teaches about the body of Christ in the context of a specific local church community. Hence Christians must participate in the life of a local church and joyfully take on their respective roles as members of the body.

Lesson 5. Fellowship ● 75

Satan’s strategy involves destroying unity among Christians. He is the author of confusion, insensitivity, and false doctrines. In the Bible, we discover the power whereby Satan's strategy can be defeated.
Question 7: What did Jesus make a request to the Father in his prayer?
John 17:11 It is the power of “one-mindedness” in the body of Christ. This unity among Christians reveals the essence of the gospel; and that essence comprises the fact that “in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself.” (2 Corinthians 5:19) Christ was indeed God in the flesh. He was, and is, one with the Father. If unity is destroyed in Christ's body, then the most powerful means of communicating the gospel to lost souls that Christ is God are destroyed. The ingredient in the church that convinces non-Christians that Jesus is God is unity—living in “such harmony with one another.” This, in a sense, represents a miracle because humans generally move toward disunity. When non-Christians see true unity and true oneness, their hearts cry out to partake of that kind of love (John 17:21).
Question 8: Read John 17. Which of the following is NOT something Jesus
prayed for in John 17:? a) That the disciples may experience his joy b) That the disciples may experience the same unity as the Father and Son c) That the disciples may have the glory the Father gave to the Son d) That the world may experience his joy, glory, and unity 3. Accept the Differences of One Another But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ's gift. (Ephesians 4:7) All believers have been made one in the body of Christ, but there is still great diversity among Christians. We must understand and accept the many differences found among the members of the body if we are to be Christ's unified body. 76 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training a. We Have Received Different Gifts Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us… (Romans 12:6a) The gift of salvation is from the one Holy Spirit, but he also gives other gifts. According to Paul, some were given the gift of teaching, others the gift of service, and some the gift of exhortation. The Holy Spirit desires these different gifts to be used in unity, for the building and edifying of the body of Christ, and not for comparing and criticizing.
Question 9: List the gifts from Romans 12:6-8.
b. We Have Been Given Different Levels of Faith Let not the one who eats despise the one who abstains, and let not the one who abstains pass judgment on the one who eats, for God has welcomed him. (Romans 14:3). If we are mature Christians, we will be sensitive toward our brothers and sisters in Christ who may not be as spiritually mature. We will be careful not to do anything that may cause them to stumble and fall into sin. If these two attitudes are working concurrently in a local body of believers, unity will emerge. c. We Have Different Personal Backgrounds After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!” (Revelation 7:9-10) Prejudice, favoritism, and discrimination in the body of Christ violate the laws of God. Furthermore, they violate the nature of the functioning body of Christ. We are all one. Every member is important—rich or poor, young or old, black or white, weak or strong, Jew or Gentile. If we show favoritism or judge people by outward appearances, we also destroy the unity, harmony, and oneness in the body of Christ which Christ and Paul both prayed and commanded.

Lesson 5. Fellowship ● 77

Ephesians 2:11-12. Cultural, racial, national, and religious barriers are broken down when people are brought near to God by the blood of Christ. Enemies may experience peace and reconciliation when they come together as members of the body of Christ. All believers have the same access to God the Father because the same Spirit dwells in them. Together, we are being built into a dwelling place of God.
Question 10: Consider and record your responses to the following: “Enemies
may experience peace and reconciliation when they come together as members of the body of Christ.” Think of an enemy you have (or had). How could being a member of the same body of Christ help you reconcile with that enemy and come back together in fellowship? 4. Love One Another A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. (John 13:34) This exhortation introduces another model by which our understanding of the functioning church is enriched. The concept of the family adds a dimension of warmth, concern and loyalty. The term “brotherly love” refers to the love that should coexist within family units. Applied to the church, it refers to the love Christians should have for each other as brothers and sisters in Christ. We are the family of God. We have all been “born again” into God's eternal family.
Question 11: How should true love be expressed? 1 John 3:18
Question 12: How did the first century church express its love? Acts 4:32
5. Edify the Church Therefore encourage one another and build one another up. (1 Thessalonians 5:11) 78 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training Paul commended the Thessalonian Christians for their concern and love for one another. They had learned the importance of mutual encouragement, exhortation, and comfort. He knew the primary means of encouragement—God's truth. “We also thank God constantly for this, that when you received the word of God, which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but as what it really is, the word of God, which is at work in you believers.” (1 Thessalonians 2:13) Christians must be ready to share the word with others who are in special need of encouragement. But we cannot encourage one another with Scripture if we are not familiar with Scripture. Therefore every believer should study the word of God, not only for their personal growth but also for assisting others in their growth. 6. Conclusion In the “body of Christ,” the church, every member must contribute to its continual growth. The church should be a group of people who believe in the word, who believe in the God of the Bible, who love and care for one another, and who want all people to be saved and experience fellowship with God and with other believers. This is what Jesus prayed during his ministry on earth. I do not ask for these only, but also for those who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me. (John 17:20-21)

And God said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth and subdue it and have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens and over every living thing that moves on the earth.’” (Genesis 1:28) This ultimate command was given to everyone—believer, unbeliever, man, woman, and child. Christians who believe in God as the Creator should wholeheartedly obey this command. After his work on the cross and then his resurrection, Jesus gave an important commission to his disciples. Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, to the end of the age. The following are the three views on the relationship between the church and the world: 1. Antagonistic view - one of confrontation 2. Mediating view - one of compromise 3. Changing view - one of conquering Among the three views, the changing view is the sound one which Christians should adopt. Christians have been called from the world to the body of Christ.

the sound one Christians should adopt. What are the dangers of antagonistic and mediating views, and why are they less appropriate for Christians? To help with your answer read Romans 12:1-2. God dwells among the people who have been sent into the world and not in buildings which are separated from the world. (Thomas Gillespie) #### B. Attitude Toward Work God does not limit his interest only to our “church” activities. He is equally interested in our painting and teaching as much as he is interested in how we pray, how we read the Bible, and how we praise him. God does not separate between the “secular” and “divine” because all things are under his authority. As God calls us into a relationship with him, we come to realize that we should use all our activities to praise God and to serve our neighbors. Instead of saying, “I am not a minister of God but a carpenter,” we should say, “I am doing the work of a disciple of Christ through carpentry.”

84 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training 4. Strategy for Witnessing Objective 3: List the strategies of witnessing you may use in different situations Jesus came to seek and to save the lost. Since he lives within us, we can simply ask him to give us the courage to speak for him. Whenever you are alone with a person for a few minutes, you can assume that you are there by divine appointment to share the good news of God's love and forgiveness. Though you should always seek to bring those who are interested to a definite commitment to Christ, you should not feel discouraged when some refuse to receive him as their Savior. That is God's responsibility. It is your responsibility to tell them the good news with love and genuine concern. We can set the following strategies according to the situation. 1. If it is difficult to have personal time, you can distribute tracks. 2. If you have 20-30 minutes of personal time, you can use Four Spiritual Laws, Bridge Analogy, Evangelization Explosion, and other tools for witnessing. 3. If you can meet on a regular basis (workplace, church, etc.), you can have a personal Bible study with Unit I of this workbook.

Witnessing as a Way of Life Objective 4: List some important points to witness by life Objective 5: Be prepared to share your salvation testimony to others Successful witnessing may be defined as simply taking the initiative to share Christ in the power of the Holy Spirit and leaving the results to God (2 Timothy 4:2; Colossians 1:28-29). Here are some important reminders as you step out in faith to communicate Jesus Christ to others in your ordinary life. 1. Be prepared. You have to be prepared for God to use you as he wants. 2. Pray in the Spirit. It is our responsibility to share Christ with others and to pray for people to come to Christ. God is the One who by his Spirit can produce faith in the hearts of men and women and change their lives. But we should not expect vague and superficial prayers to be answered. We should pray with an earnest love and desire for their salvation. Pray by mentioning their names individually and record when and how God answered your prayer. 3. Take the initiative. Regard the opportunities you have of meeting people as divine appointments. Consider the following: a) Do not wait for people to come to you. Go to them with the good news of Christ. God has already commanded us to go and tell the good news to all. b) We witness because it is the command of Christ but we should go further and make witnessing a regular part of our lives. As you come into contact with and meet people, witness to them. Show them your concern for them and naturally lead the conversation. The words Jesus said to 86 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training the woman at the well (John 4:7) and what Philip said to the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:30) are good examples. 4. Turn the conversation to Christ. Do not be too hasty! We need to show genuine interest in the person by listening to what he or she thinks or believes about the meaning and purpose of life. As we do this it opens the door to share about how Jesus gives meaning and purpose to our lives. 5. Expect results. When you witness, expect people to respond. We should not base our expectation on our technique or beliefs but place our confidence in his love, his power, and his promise.

Defining Being Filled with the Spirit Objective 1: Explain what being filled with the Holy Spirit means The Holy Spirit dwells in every believer. The Holy Spirit causes us to be “born again” and empowers us to live a Christ-centered life. We cannot, through our own efforts, lead a Christ-centered life. We must ask, trust, and depend on the Holy Spirit to lead and guide us through our journey as Christians. This is called the Spirit-filled life.
Question 1: Read John 14:16-17. Before Jesus left this earth what did he
promise to the disciples?
Question 2: In John 14:18, Jesus says that he would not leave them as
orphans but would come to them. What do you think this means in relation to the promise he made?
Question 3: In John 15:26, what does Jesus say about the ministry of the Holy
Spirit?
Question 4: What explanation does Jesus give in John 16:14 regarding the
Spirit’s work?
Question 5: Having answered the preceding questions, how would you
summarize the primary ministry of the Holy Spirit? The word “filled” actually means to be directed and empowered by the Spirit. Since the Holy Spirit came to glorify Christ (John 16:14) and is the Spirit of Christ (Romans 8:9), to be filled with the Spirit is to be filled with or abiding in Christ. To abide in Christ is to live in dependence upon him, recognizing that it is his life, his wisdom, his resources, his strength, and his ability operating through you, which enables you to live according

Lesson 7. The Spirit-Filled Life ● 89

to his will. Christ lives in us and expresses his life through us by the power of his Spirit.
Question 6: Ephesians 5:18 contrasts being filled with the Spirit to getting
drunk with wine. What kind of state is to be filled with the Holy Spirit? To be filled with the Spirit does not mean to be in a mystical state. Nor does it mean to be in an emotionally dry or highly intellectual state. The concept of the filling of the Holy Spirit from this verse stresses the abiding influence and power that the presence of the Spirit of Christ has in our lives and on our character. #### B. Reasons to Be Filled with the Spirit Objective 2: List some reasons why you need to be filled with the Holy Spirit As long as we are in this world and in our flesh, we cannot keep from sinning. Even if we believe in Jesus Christ and have begun a new life, we are still able to fall into sinful behavior (1 John 1:8). That is why the apostle Paul cried out, “Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of death?” (Romans 7:24)
Question 7: How does Galatians 5:17 describe this conflict?
A natural person can sometimes overcome this conflict with conscientious thoughts or ethical actions. However in our own power alone, we will fail spiritually. Our old selves cannot win this conflict because of our fleshly desires.
Question 8: Read Romans 8:9-10, 13-14. What do Christians have to do to
win this conflict between the flesh and the Spirit? Each person who claims to walk with Christ must be filled with the Holy Spirit continuously—this leads to a victorious life. 90 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training #### C. Results of Being Filled with the Spirit Objective 3: Identify some expectations of being filled with the Holy Spirit In order to live a victorious life, we must be filled with the Holy Spirit. We cannot overcome the power of Satan by ourselves. However through the power of the Holy Spirit we are able to overcome the power of Satan. We have already learned that the primary ministry of the Holy Spirit is to reveal Jesus to us. The Holy Spirit impacts our lives by showing us who Jesus is. As we focus on Jesus, we are able to become more like him.
Question 9: Find the image of Jesus from Galatians 5:22-23 by listing the fruit
of the Spirit. Through Jesus Christ, we can have victory over sin. Jesus himself lived a sinless life giving us the perfect example of how to live. It is important to build his character into our lives through the ministry of the Spirit so that we might live in a way that reflects Jesus.
Question 10: We are meant to feel the impossibility of living the victorious life
in the strength of our flesh. When we try, we fail over and over. Recall a time when you failed to live up to God’s standards; then record why you think you failed. What can you do next time to live victoriously? #### D. Way of Being Filled with the Spirit Objective 4: Describe how you can be filled with the Holy Spirit Objective 5: Renew your mind to maintain the filling of the Holy Spirit We have already learned that the filling of the Spirit emphasizes the abiding influence and power that his presence has in our lives and on our character. Nobody is able to change his or her character immediately. It takes time. As time goes by, our character should be transformed to that of Jesus. There is no single formula that can fill us with the Holy Spirit instantaneously. By having fellowship with the Holy Spirit, however, we can be gradually transformed into Jesus’ image.

Satan's Use of Temptation Objective 4: List the three ways Satan attacks you, understand the strategies against the attacks, and use this information to live a victorious life The ultimate source of all evil is Satan. But that does not mean that the devil always attacks us personally. Satan attacks us using every possible means including his direct involvement. We are attacked through three basic channels which Scripture calls the devil, the world, and the flesh. It is crucial, when you are being tempted, to determine what kind of temptation it is because each should be handled differently. 96 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training 1. Attacks Us Directly Scripture teaches that there is one personal supernatural spirit known as the devil or Satan, and there are many fallen angels known as the devil’s angels, or demons. This devil attacks directly to shake our relationship with God. When you are tempted to deny God's goodness, God's word, and/or God’s faithfulness, these are attacks directed at your God- awareness.
Question 9: How did Satan attack Judas Iscariot? Luke 22:3; John 13:2
How does one handle a direct demonic attack upon God-awareness? First of all, one needs to acknowledge that the devil exists, and then one has to resist the devil (James 4:7). Let us study the best ways to resist the devil. Christ gave us the perfect example of how to resist the devil.
Question 10: In Matthew 4:4, 7, 10, what did Jesus use to resist the devil?
Jesus responded with the sword of the Spirit—the word of God. This is the best way to resist the devil. If the devil tempts you to doubt your salvation, you may rebuke his lies with the truth that leads to eternal life (John 5:24; 1 John 5:13). Knowing and studying the Bible are so important, especially in dealing with temptations. That is why memorizing Scripture is also important. David said, “I have stored up your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.” (Psalm 119:11) The more you study and master the word, the more you will be prepared to effectively deal with this type of temptation. 2. Through the World Satan not only attacks us directly, but also indirectly through the world. The kind of world we are talking about is “the world” God mentioned in 1 John 2:15-16 and “this world” mentioned in Romans 12:2. This kind of world refers to the world of unsaved people and the society, culture, and value systems they have established. The subtlest kinds of temptations are from this channel.
Question 11: The world tempts us in what three areas? What are specific
examples of these? 1 John 2:16

Lesson 8. Temptation ● 97

An example: A young couple is very zealous for the Lord and then suddenly stops attending church. They purchased a new home and are now so busy decorating it that they have no time for God. They actually love the house more than they love God. That is sin and idolatry! The most difficult type of temptation comes from the world. How does one handle this type of temptation? Read Matthew 6:19- 34. Probably this type of temptation—the world attacking the soul—will be the most prominent over the period of your life span. This is particularly true in our materialistic society. Suppose as a woman, you find yourself enamored with the latest fashions. It becomes an inordinate passion that is always on your mind. Clothes! Clothes! Clothes! Or a man gets intense car fever. Cars! Cars! Cars! If you begin to let your love for God grow cold, then the world will suck you into its vacuum. These kinds of temptations cannot be overcome by escaping (John 17:15). When you are tempted by the world, check your relationship with the Lord rather than fighting back. That is, examine your devotional life.
Question 12: Think about each area of your devotional life.
a) Quiet Time: b) Prayer: When you get back to your devotional life and renew your love for God, you will not love this world. Then, the satanic attack through this world loses its power. 3. Through the Desires of Our Flesh Satan attacks through the basic desires of the flesh that everyone has. If the temptation through the world is an attack from the outside of our body, the temptation of the desire of the flesh is an attack from the inside of our body. The body or flesh, which is created by God, is not evil in itself. Therefore biological desires are not evil either. However some temptations are directed right at the biological desires of the body such as sex or eating. A Christian is constantly tempted to misuse and misdirect these biological desires that God has given each person. 98 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training

It is important that we strive to avoid such temptations.

Have Quiet Time regularly. 99 100 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training The tragedy of the modern church is that there are many who are called to faith, but few who are called to obedience. Faith that perseveres against the temptations of Satan through a Spirit-filled life is very precious. A willingness to follow and obey Jesus is needed for Christians to keep their faith actively working for God. To do his work, it is important first to follow him. Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. (Matthew 4:19) Following Jesus means that I accept his plans and perfect will. It also means I need to give my life unconditionally to him and obey him. #### A. Meaning of Obedience and Basic Attitude Objective 1: Describe the meaning of obedience Objective 2: Understand the basic attitude of obedience toward the Lord
Question 1: Read Luke 5:1-11. How did Peter show his obedience to Jesus?
v 5 A decision to obey Christ can greatly impact our future. By obeying, Peter came to know Jesus and later became the head disciple. When we obey him in the small things that occur in our lives, our lives will be transformed more to his likeness.
Question 2: What attitudes should Christians have in order to completely
obey Christ? a) Toward Jesus (Matthew 28:18) b) Toward oneself (Romans 12:1) c) Toward the relationship between oneself and Jesus (Luke 9:23)

Lesson 9. Obedience ● 101

We need to know God and acknowledge his authority in order to lead a life of obedience. We are called to say “no” to our selfish desires and attitude and “yes” to the will of Christ. We are called to dedicate our lives to Christ and to offer our bodies as living sacrifices to him.
Question 3: Meditate on Romans 12:1. Paul’s exhortation to this church is
based on all of his previous teachings up through chapter 11. This teaching includes God’s gracious salvation from the penalty of sin plus provision for victory over sin after salvation—even the fullness of salvation that will still come to Israel when God fulfills his promises! Paul calls this directive in Romans 12:1 to present our bodies as a holy sacrifice to God our “acceptable service.” Considering all the wonderful mercies that God has shown to you through Jesus Christ, record your response to this command to offer your body to the Lord daily as a living sacrifice, including any and all reservations you might feel. When people go up in a balloon, they take bags of sand as weights. When they want to go higher, they throw some of those bags overboard. The more they throw out, the higher they go. Our Christian walk is the same. The more of the things of the flesh, the world, and the devil we throw overboard, the higher we will rise in the heights of spiritual blessings. #### B. Areas and Objects of Obedience Objective 3: Notice the importance of obedience to the Lord in your life Objective 4: Explain the relationship between obedience and suffering Objective 5: List some authorities you should obey
Question 4: What areas of their lives should the disciples of Christ deny in
order to follow Jesus? Find three areas from Luke 14:25-27, 33. 102 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training
Question 5: From the previous question, think and record your thoughts of
areas in your life that you may be struggling to give up to follow Christ. Then evaluate why these areas are more difficult to give up than others. What about them is attractive to you? Obeying Christ in the area of physical possessions is a very important part of obedience in a Christian's life. When Jesus commanded the rich young man to sell all of his possessions and give them to the poor, Jesus was not asking him to become poor, but was looking for complete obedience (Mark 10:17-22). Especially in a world obsessed with materialism, there is no better scale for measuring our degree of obedience than our attitude towards material things. Christians’ obedience in this area is not only shown by giving and helping the poor, but is more deeply related to what attitude they have toward material possessions. Christians cannot be regarded as totally obedient in this area if they spend their money excessively for themselves while not helping the less fortunate. Obedience is not only keeping his words and denying oneself. We must obey him in all areas of our lives even while suffering is present in our lives.

behave because of this? a) Ecclesiastes 7:14 b) Job 2:10 c) Genesis 50:20

Question 7: What attitude should obedient Christians have when confronted
by suffering? a) Philippians 1:29 b) Romans 8:17-18 c) Mark 10:32-34 d) John 12:24 Obedient death is necessary for Christians to bear fruit (Mark 8:34-36). This death means the death of our self-esteem, privilege, prejudice, ambitions, and our comfort. The absolute authority for obedience for Christians is, of course, Jesus Christ. However as people living within a family, a church, and a community, Christians have other authorities to obey.

There are some instances when we have to disobey them in order to obey Jesus (Acts 4:19). #### C. 1. Take sermon notes during a worship service. 2. Read 1 and 2 Peter. 3. Study this lesson. 4. Memorize 1 Corinthians 3:9; 1 Peter 2:9- 10. 5. Have Quiet Time regularly. 6. Be ready to take the final exam. 7. Write a testimony about this training program. 107 108 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. (Matthew 4:19) To do the works of Jesus Christ, we must have a deeper fellowship with him and follow him. The training we have received so far shows its fruit in characteristic development and in the Lord's ministry. In this lesson we will study about the ministry. There are still many people in churches who think they are living a Christian life by just listening to sermons from worship services. They have this passive attitude toward their life of faith because they have not been trained properly as Jesus’ disciples. When believers are trained, their attitude becomes more active. Therefore the fruit of training will result in the ministry for the Lord. If the Reformation of the sixteenth century gave the Bible back to the church members, the spiritual reformation that is to come will return ministry to the church members. Francis Aeris said the following: If we have been baptized, we are ministers whether we have been ordained as priests or not. In this lesson we will look at five important elements to help the believers better understand their role in ministry. We will examine a biblical view of (1) the church, (2) the believers, (3) the gifts of God, (4) training, and (5) the world. An understanding of these five elements will greatly assist believers to be spiritually effective in ministry. #### A. Biblical View of the Church Objective 1: Describe the biblical basis of the church with a couple of supporting verses The most challenging fact to Christians is not that I am to do something for the church but that I constitute the church. (F. C. Mather) In describing the relationship between the believers and the church, it is incorrect to say that the believers are “in” the church. It is equally wrong to say that the believers work “for” the church. Also, it is not biblical to say that believers work “in” the church.
Question 1: What is the biblical expression describing the relationship
between the believers and the church? Ephesians 2:20-22

Lesson 10. Ministry ● 109

Believers themselves “are” the church. So in order to know the believers’ ministry, it is necessary to know the ministry of the church. The two elements that make the church are service and fellowship. The church needs to carry out the ministries that Jesus did while he was on the earth in order to function as the body of Christ.
Question 2: Summarize the ministry of Jesus from Matthew 4:23. How is each
related to the commission given to the church? a) _______________ (Teaching, training, and spiritual arming) b) _______________ (Spreading the gospel, foreign mission) c) _______________ (Social service, participation in world) All ministries should begin at the church which represents the body of Christ. Ministry should be conducted by individual members for individuals and to individuals, and should be transmitted to those outside the church as well. Therefore the church must carry out these three ministries—teaching, preaching, and healing—when members gather together. Individuals must carry out these duties in the world as they are dispersed in the world. #### B. Biblical View of the Believers Objective 2: Explain the importance of believers to fulfilling the commission of Jesus Christ We often hear people saying, “But I am only a member of this church.” This might sound very humble, but they have not properly understood the commission of Jesus. The Bible tells us that every Christian is a minister. Church members are not the objects of ministry, as is often understood, but are the subjects of church ministry. What is Christian ministry? For the next four questions, fill in the blanks with appropriate words.

5:14).

(Matthew 9:38). Churches cannot spread the gospel because they are too separated from their neighbors and are introverted. Church is outside the world, contrary to what the Bible wants. The Bible teaches us that Christians should be inside the world. As Jesus, the head of the church, did, the church should be incarnate in the ignorant, filthy, and sinful cities and towns in which they exist. (Donald McGavran)

#### C. Biblical View of the Gifts of God Objective 3: List the spiritual gifts from the Bible and know what gifts you have God commands us to do his ministry, but he also gives us the gifts that we need in order to carry out his ministry. We should neither be proud of them as if they were ours, nor should we fail to use them. Gifts are freely given by God for his ministry. Gifts are to be used for the glory of God.

gift(s) to use and that we are to be using that gift(s) accordingly. Record your thoughts on what gift(s) you may have. How can you find a way to practice your gift to edify others? #### D. Biblical View of Training 112 ● One-to-One Discipleship Training Objective 4: Indicate what training is necessary to be a good worker for the Lord Gifts are essential to do the ministry of God. But for that gift to bear fruit, training is needed. It is wrong for a church to give someone an important role without training that person first. Those who desire to serve God should make necessary preparations. Training that is in line with the gift becomes an appropriate preparation for the church ministry. Two inherent problems that our churches have are (1) there are not many pastors who want to train the believers and (2) there are few believers who desire to receive training. Some people think training is difficult and still others think that it is unnecessary. However the training for believers is imperative for a church to become a fully functioning, spiritually effective church.
Question 11: How did Jesus train his disciples (Mark 3:13-15)? How can this
be applied to the church today? a) Calling and appointing: b) Making them be with him: c) Sending them out to preach: There are several fields in which believers should be trained. 1. Devotional: Spending time with God, memorizing verses, etc. 2. Evangelism: Personal evangelism, evangelical Bible study, etc. 3. Encouragement: Building up and edification 4. Counseling: Family, marriage, adolescent, etc. Consider the following suggestions for an effective training. 1. Never lose the commission as a worker 2. Look for people who are ministering with similar gifts 3. Read and study the Bible and other books which are necessary for ministry 4. Think of ways of using the gifts you have received 5. Start humbly even though you might have much experience

Lesson 10. Ministry ● 113

in church life 6. Join a group that will challenge you in your dedication
Question 12: Review the two lists. Write and explain how you will further your
development in these areas. #### E. Biblical View of the World Objective 5: Find what you can do in this world, as a disciple of Jesus, to fulfill his commission For trained believers to minister, they need to understand their field of ministry. Many Christians limit the scope of ministry to inside the church. But the field of our ministry is this world. The world in which we live and work is where we should minister. Many believers limit their field to the region or country they belong to. But our scope of ministry is to the end of the earth (Acts 1:8). By broadening our vision of the world, it helps us to have a greater sense of God’s heart for the whole world.

ministry?

The gospel must be spread to all regions of the world, and the name of Jesus must be heralded. The everyday work we do during weekdays is also an act of worship to God. Our work becomes a living worship when we do everything within a right relationship with God.
